question.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=6t-2$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=-1\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=1\,\text{s}$, calculate the speed of the particle at the moment $t=3\,\text{s}.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (6t-2)\text{d}t \\  & =3{t}^{2}-2t+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(1)=-1.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-1 & =3(1)^{2}-2(1)+C \\ -1 & =3-2+C \\ C & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=3{t}^{2}-2t-2.$

We evaluate the velocity at time $t=3\,\text{s}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(3) & =3(3)^{2}-2(3)-2 \\  & =27-6-2 \\  & =19\,\text{m/s}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the speed is equal to $|v(t)|,$ we conclude that the speed of the particle is $19\,\text{m/s}.$
